chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn Mahdi) from Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Baghdadi) from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shumman from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'Indeed, the servant stands in prayer at night, and sleep overcomes him, swaying him right and left, with his chin resting on his chest. Then Allah, the Exalted, commands the gates of heaven to open, and He says to the angels: 'Look at My servant; what is befalling him in his approach to Me through what I have not made obligatory upon him, hoping for something from Me of three matters: a sin I forgive him, or a repentance I renew for him, or sustenance I increase for him. Bear witness, O My angels, that I have gathered all three for him.'

key_terms.التَّقَرُّبِ: Approaching or drawing near to God

ai.seo_question: What rewards does Allah grant to a servant who prays at night even when sleepy?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* emphasizes the divine attention paid to voluntary night prayers (Tahajjud), where Allah commands the gates of heaven to open for the dozing worshipper. It underscores the merit of supererogatory acts by promising three specific spiritual benefits: the forgiveness of sins, the renewal of repentance, and an increase in sustenance (rizq). This narrative illustrates the concept of 'Ibadah al-Tatawwu' as a means of drawing closer to God beyond the obligatory duties.
